extracted.intended_audience: appellants (patent applicants), patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and pro se appellants preparing appeal briefs to the USPTO Board
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting and filing an appeal brief under 37 CFR 41.37 for an appeal to the USPTO Board (BPAI/PTAB), including required contents, appendices, format, and procedural compliance. Covers required statements, argument structure, and appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 and fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any brief filed on or after September 13, 2004 must comply with the requirements set forth in 37 CFR 41.37 and be accompanied by the fee under 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2). Briefs filed (or with a certificate of mailing date) before that date must comply with either former 37 CFR 1.192 or 37 CFR 41.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required. If certificate of mailing date is prior to Sept 13, 2004, older rule may apply. Noncompliance can cause the brief to be held defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Technology Center and control number on all documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief, as well as every other document relating to an appeal, should indicate the number of the Technology Center (TC) to which the application or patent under reexamination is assigned and the application or reexamination control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including TC and control number on each paper helps proper routing and handling by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to each ground of rejection presented
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant's brief must be responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner that the appellant is presenting for review in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a ground of rejection stated by the examiner is not addressed in the appellant's brief, that ground of rejection will be summarily sustained by the Board. Oral argument will not remedy such a deficiency. Appellant must point out reasons for believing a ground is improper rather than assuming the Board will infer them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief must set forth authorities and arguments and fully state appellant's position
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule requires that the brief must set forth the authorities and arguments relied upon and must provide the Board with a brief fully stating the position of the appellant with respect to each ground of rejection presented for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief should be self-contained so no search of the record is required to determine appellant's position; it should not incorporate or reference previous responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and order of required items (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must have all of the required items under appropriate headings in the order indicated in 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1). The headings are required even when an item is not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there is no information related to the section heading, the word 'none' should be used under the heading. Failure to include required items or headings will be treated as a defect and the Office will notify appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro se exception for required items
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application or reexamination proceeding is being prosecuted pro se (no attorney or agent of record) and the brief was neither prepared nor signed by a registered practitioner, the brief which does not contain all items (i) to (x) will be accepted as long as it substantially complies with items (i)–(iv) and (vii)–(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro se appellants have limited relief but still must include the core items—real party in interest, related proceedings, status of claims, status of amendments, argument, and appendices as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide copies of relied references in evidence appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: If in the brief appellant relies on some reference, appellant is expected to provide the Board with a copy of it in the evidence appendix of the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of references relied on by appellant allow the Board to consider the authorities without having to find them elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by name the real party in interest even if the party named in the caption is the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant does not name the real party in interest, the Office will notify appellant of the defect and give time to file an amended brief; failure to correct will result in dismissal of the appeal. Identification is required so Board members can avoid conflicts of interest. Example wording: 'The real party in interest is XXXX corporation, the assignee of record, which is a subsidiary of a joint venture between YYYY corporation and ZZZZ corporation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals and interferences (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying all prior and pending appeals, judicial proceedings or interferences known to appellant which may be related to, directly affect or be directly affected by or have a bearing on the Board's decision in the pending appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify related proceedings by application number, patent number, appeal number or interference number; requirement extends to commonly owned applications with common subject matter or common priority. Copies of decisions rendered in those proceedings must be included in the related proceedings appendix. If none, omission will be presumed to mean 'none.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of all the claims in the application or patent under reexamination; for each claim appellant must state whether it is canceled, allowed or confirmed, rejected, withdrawn, objected to, etc.; each claim on appeal must be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids confusion as to which claims are on appeal and the precise wording of those claims, particularly where claims were amended after final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of any amendment filed subsequent to final rejection, i.e., whether or not the amendment has been acted upon by the examiner, and if so, whether it was entered or denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement should reflect the appellant's understanding; appellants are encouraged to check the Office's PAIR system for up-to-date status. Including items (iii) and (iv) helps resolve disagreements before the Board considers the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each of the independent claims involved in the appeal, which must refer to the specification by page and line number, and to the drawing, if any, by reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each independent claim and each dependent claim argued separately, every means-plus-function and step-plus-function element (35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph) must be identified and the corresponding structure, material, or acts in the specification set forth with page/line and drawing references. Failure to provide this summary will result in Office notice to amend the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise statement of each ground of rejection presented for review; the statement must be specific (e.g., 'unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Smith in view of Jones'), and must not include argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement such as 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable' is insufficient. Do not include arguments here; arguments belong in the Argument section. Each ground must be separately stated under its own heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant's contentions with respect to each ground of rejection presented and the basis for those contentions, including citations of authorities, statutes, and parts of the record relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simply pointing out what a claim recites is not an argument for patentability. 'Any arguments or authorities not included in the brief or reply brief filed pursuant to § 41.41 will be refused consideration by the Board, unless good cause is shown.' Arguments made first at oral hearing are not normally entitled to consideration. A supplemental paper is allowed only if new, relevant authority becomes available after filing. Each ground of rejection must be treated under a separate heading; claims may be argued separately or grouped, but grouping can waive argument for individual claims. Best practice: include a subheading for each claim you want separately considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy should be a clean copy without markings (unless reissue/reexamination contexts permit). The copy of claims should be double-spaced and the appendix should start on a new page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing copies of any evidence submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131, or 1.132 or of any other evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon by appellant in the appeal, along with a statement setting forth where in the record that evidence was entered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted in the brief. The appendix should start on a new page. If there is no evidence being relied upon by appellant, include an evidence appendix with the indication 'none.' See 37 CFR 41.33 for evidence submitted after appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related proceedings appendix (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing copies of decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified pursuant to (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix should start on a new page. If there are no such copies being submitted, include a related proceedings appendix with the indication 'none.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum requirements and permissive inclusion of other material
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) specifies the minimum required items for a brief but does not prohibit inclusion of other material which appellant considers necessary or desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A brief is in compliance as long as it includes items (i)–(x) in the order set forth. Additional useful materials may include a list of references, table of contents, table of cases, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new or non-admitted amendments or evidence in brief (37 CFR 41.37(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(2) prohibits inclusion in a brief of any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to introduce new matter or evidence in the brief; evidence submitted after appeal has specific treatment under 37 CFR 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended example format and content (example items A–L)
rubrics_metrics.description: An example brief format: (A) Identification page; (B) Table of Contents; (C) Real party in interest; (D) Related appeals and interferences; (E) Status of claims; (F) Status of amendments; (G) Summary of claimed subject matter; (H) Grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal; (I) Argument; (J) Claims appendix; (K) Evidence appendix; (L) Related proceedings appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item should start on a separate page. This example illustrates a practical ordering and pagination consistent with 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief must be directed to claims and record as of time of appeal; withdrawal of claims permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must be directed to the claims and to the record of the case as they appeared at the time of the appeal, but appellant may withdraw from consideration on appeal any claims or issues as desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if appellant withdraws claims or acquiesces to a rejection, the examiner must continue to make the rejection in the examiner's answer unless an amendment obviating the rejection has been entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filed brief referred to examiner and possible examiner actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A timely filed brief will be referred to the examiner for consideration and preparation of an examiner's answer if the brief is proper and the application is not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's answer may withdraw the rejection of claims, and may determine that it is necessary to reopen prosecution to enter a new ground of rejection (see MPEP § 1207.04).
